newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds and futures begin upward trek again.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds and futures begin upward trek again.

text.p: German Bunds and futures started another session in positive ground, buoyed by strong U.S. Treasuries overnight and determined to plot a path higher.

Analysts said that while the September contract had a little work to do after failing to close above the 102.92 level on Wednesday, it looked likely that this first barrier would be overcome swiftly and the contract would retrace Wednesday's steps and push on through to 103.00 and beyond.
By 0627 GMT, the DTB September future was six basis points higher, challenging the 102.92 level. In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark was at 103.38 for a 5.54 percent bid yield.

With no economic data on the horizon this session, analysts said the main focus for the market would be the Bundesbank's council meeting and a news conference scheduled to be held afterwards at 1015 GMT.
But the meeting, the only one in the year be held out of town, is unikely to bring about any change in interest rates.

Some traders said the market was slightly unsettled late on Wednesday by rumours that the Bundesbank might switch back to a variable repo rate, but the talk was dismissed with players putting it down to a lack of real news in the market and the usual pick-up in tension before a Bundesbank meeting.
"Nobody really thinks they're going to move rates," said one Frankfurt-based trader. "The market was just looking for something to talk about."
A poll conducted by Reuters showed all 10 economists asked said they expected no change in monetary policy.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Wednesday that although price pressure appeared to be more under control than for many years, vigilance on inflation was still necessary.
"These are fairly standard comments which do not herald any policy change," an analyst at MMS Europe said in a morning research note.
